test_title: SSC CGL Tier-II (AAO) 2023 Official Paper-III (Held On: 27 Oct, 2023 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Under monopoly market, if the seller charges different prices from different customers on the basis of paying capacity of the consumer, it is said to be price discrimination of the ________.
solution:
The correct answer is** price discrimination of the first degree.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Price discrimination of the first degree:**

 
 
• Also known as perfect price discrimination, it occurs when a monopolist charges each consumer their maximum willingness to pay.
 
• This method allows the seller to capture the entire consumer surplus, converting it into additional revenue.
 
• It requires detailed knowledge of each consumer's willingness to pay, which can be challenging to obtain and implement.
 
• In practice, examples include personalized pricing in online markets or auctions where each bid reflects the buyer's highest valuation.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Second-degree price discrimination:**

 
 
• Incorrect in this context. This type involves charging different prices based on the quantity consumed or the version of the product. Examples include bulk discounts or different versions of software with varying features.
 
 
 
• **Third-degree price discrimination:**
 
 
• Incorrect here. It involves segmenting the market into distinct groups based on identifiable characteristics like age, location, or time of purchase, and charging each group a different price. Common examples are student discounts or senior citizen discounts.
 
 
 
• **Fourth-degree price discrimination:**
 
 
• This is not a standard term in economic theory. The recognized forms of price discrimination are primarily the first, second, and third degrees.
